observation.visible_scene: A blue soccer ball with silver-grey panels and a small printed logo sits centered on a cylindrical base wrapped in yellow-and-black diagonal hazard tape, which rests on a wooden table against a plain grey wall. Above the ball is a flat grey press plate attached to a vertical metallic cylinder, initially just touching the ball's top. A red seven-segment digital readout is overlaid in the top-right corner (partly cropped at the right edge).
visible_changes: The upper press plate moves steadily downward across the clip, pressing into the ball.

The ball deforms under the load: its top flattens against the plate, its vertical height decreases, and it bulges slightly wider at the sides, while its bottom stays in contact with the hazard-taped platform.
The digital counter rises overall from about 10 to about 21, with small non-monotonic fluctuations (e.g. brief dips back to 12 between 13 and 14).
The ball remains intact throughout the excerpt; no burst, puncture, or release of pressure is seen.
The base platform, table, and wall stay fixed in the frame, indicating the visible motion is the plate descending and the ball compressing rather than the objects translating.
outside_clip_unknowns: The physical meaning/units of the digital counter (pressure, force, or something else) is not shown.
What happens after the last frame (whether the ball eventually bursts or the plate retracts) is unseen.
The state before t=0 (how the plate reached contact, the ball's initial inflation) is unseen.
Any operator or control mechanism driving the press is not visible.
uncertain_details: A very slight apparent enlargement of the ball/base between early and late frames may be a slow camera zoom-in or just compression-induced size change; background cues are too weak to confirm camera motion.
Exact counter digits are partly clipped at the right edge in some frames, so values are read as best-effort.
Whether the plate was already in light contact at the first frame or just about to touch is ambiguous.
